newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PERSETEL JUMPS AFTER Q-DATA MERGER.
newsitem.headline: PERSETEL JUMPS AFTER Q-DATA MERGER.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Persetel Holdings rose in brisk trade on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange after it announced on Thursday a merger with electronics firm Q-Data Holdings Ltd, dealers and analysts said on Friday.
Persetel added 130 cents to 36.25 rand in trade worth 17 million rand and Q-Data shares fell 75 cents to 10.15 rand in a volume worth 2.6 million rand.
The companies said on Thursday Persetel would buy all of Q-Data's businesses and merge with their own.
It would pay for the assets by issuing some 60 million new Persetel shares to current Q-Data shareholders in the ratio of 281 new Persetel Q-Data shares for every 1,000 Q-Data shares held.
"If you do the calculations... one would expect Q-Data to come down and Persetel to move up," an analyst said.

She said, assuming Thursday's closing prices of 35 rand for Persetel and 10.90 rand for Q-data, the ratios showed that 281 multiplied by 35 rand divided by 1,000 equals 9.84, which is the Q-Data imputed price.
And doing the calculations vice-versa resulted in a price of 38.80 rand for Persetel.
"You should not expect the prices to come to exactly those levels, but it does indicate that Persetel should go up and Q-data come down," she said.
The merged company, to be called Persetel Q-Data (PQ) Holdings, would have an expected market capitalisation of 12 billion rand, making it the 22nd largest company on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
